claim: mir-17-92 is a potent polycistronic oncomir that encodes six mature miRNAs.
source: mir-17-92, a potent polycistronic oncomir, encodes six mature miRNAs with complex modes of interactions.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract and supported by Figure 1A showing the gene structure.

claim: In the Eμ-myc Burkitt's lymphoma model, mir-17-92 exhibits potent oncogenic activity by repressing c-Myc-induced apoptosis, primarily through its miR-19 components.
source: In the Eμ-myc Burkitt's lymphoma model, mir-17-92 exhibits potent oncogenic activity by repressing c-Myc-induced apoptosis, primarily through its miR-19 components.
evidence: Stated in abstract and supported by experimental data in adoptive transfer experiments.

claim: mir-17-92 encodes the miR-92 component that negatively regulates its oncogenic cooperation with c-Myc.
source: Surprisingly, mir-17-92 also encodes the miR-92 component that negatively regulates its oncogenic cooperation with c-Myc.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated by survival data showing mir-17-92Δ92 accelerates tumor onset compared to intact mir-17-92.

claim: The miR-92 effect is mediated by its direct repression of Fbw7.
source: This miR-92 effect is, at least in part, mediated by its direct repression of Fbw7, which promotes the proteosomal degradation of c-Myc.
evidence: Stated in abstract and supported by luciferase reporter assays and protein level measurements.

claim: Overexpressing miR-92 leads to aberrant c-Myc increase.
source: Thus, overexpressing miR-92 leads to aberrant c-Myc increase, imposing a strong coupling between excessive proliferation and p53-dependent apoptosis.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated by western blot data in Figure 5A.

claim: miR-92 antagonizes the oncogenic miR-19 miRNAs.
source: Interestingly, miR-92 antagonizes the oncogenic miR-19 miRNAs; and such functional interaction coordinates proliferation and apoptosis during c-Myc-induced oncogenesis.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated by apoptosis assays showing miR-19 dampens miR-92-induced apoptosis.

claim: The miR-19:miR-92 antagonism is disrupted in B-lymphoma cells that favor a greater increase of miR-19 over miR-92.
source: This miR-19:miR-92 antagonism is disrupted in B-lymphoma cells that favor a greater increase of miR-19 over miR-92.
evidence: Stated in abstract and supported by real-time PCR data in Figure 7A-B showing differential expression.

claim: mir-17-92 genomic amplification and aberrant overexpression have been observed in many human tumors including Burkitt's lymphoma, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), and lung cancer.
source: One of the best example is mir-17-92, a potent oncomir (i.e., miRNA oncogene), whose genomic amplification and aberrant overexpression have been observed in many human tumors including Burkitt's lymphoma, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), and lung cancer (Lu et al., 2005; Mendell, 2008).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: mir-17-92 regulates multiple cellular processes during tumor development, including proliferation, survival, angiogenesis, differentiation, and metastasis.
source: mir-17-92 regulates multiple cellular processes during tumor development, including proliferation, survival, angiogenesis, differentiation, and metastasis (He et al., 2007; Uziel et al., 2009; Conkrite et al., 2011; Nittner et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: mir-17-92 produces a single precursor that yields six individual mature miRNAs.
source: As a polycistronic oncomir, mir-17-92 produces a single precursor that yields six individual mature miRNAs (Figure 1A, Figure1—figure supplement 1A) (Tanzer and Stadler, 2004).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1A and cited literature.

claim: The six mir-17-92 components are categorized into four miRNA families based on seed sequence homology.
source: Based on the seed sequence homology, the six mir-17-92 components are categorized into four miRNA families (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A): miR-17 (miR-17 and 20), miR-18, miR-19 (miR-19a and 19b), and miR-92a (we will designate miR-92a as miR-92 in the remainder of our paper).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: miR-92 has a more ancient evolutionary history compared to the other mir-17-92 components.
source: Interestingly, miR-92 has a more ancient evolutionary history compared to the other mir-17-92 components (Tanzer and Stadler, 2004).
evidence: Stated with citation to prior literature.

claim: miR-92 is evolutionarily conserved in vertebrates, chordates, and invertebrates, while the remaining mir-17-92 components are only found in vertebrates.
source: miR-92 is evolutionarily conserved in vertebrates, chordates, and invertebrates, while the remaining mir-17-92 components are only found in vertebrates (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: The Eμ-myc mice carry a c-myc transgene downstream of the immunoglobulin (Ig) heavy chain enhancer Eμ.
source: The Eμ-myc mice carry a c-myc transgene downstream of the immunoglobulin (Ig) heavy chain enhancer Eμ (Langdon, 1986; Adams et al., 1985), which functionally resembles the Ig-MYC translocations that occur frequently in Burkitt's lymphomas (Tagawa et al., 2007).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: c-Myc-induced apoptosis enables a self-defense mechanism against malignant transformation, producing B-lymphomas with a late onset.
source: Thus, c-Myc-induced apoptosis enables a self-defense mechanism against malignant transformation, producing B-lymphomas with a late onset (Lowe et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated with citation to prior literature.

claim: Overexpression of mir-17-92 in Eμ-myc/+ HSPCs resulted in a considerable acceleration in tumor onset compared to the Eμ-myc/MSCV control mice.
source: When Eμ-myc/+ HSPCs were infected with MSCV (murine stem cell virus) retrovirus to overexpress the intact mir-17-92 oncomir, we observed a considerable acceleration in tumor onset compared to the Eμ-myc/MSCV control mice (p<0.01, Figure 1C).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1C showing survival curves.

claim: The oncogenic cooperation between c-Myc and mir-17-92 was significantly stronger when miR-92 was deleted within this oncomir.
source: Unexpectedly, the oncogenic cooperation between c-Myc and mir-17-92 was significantly stronger when miR-92 was deleted within this oncomir (Figure 1C).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1C showing survival data.

claim: The average survival of Eμ-myc/17-92Δ92 mice was 66 days, significantly shorter than that of Eμ-myc/17-92 mice (112 days, p<0.0001).
source: The average survival of Eμ-myc/17-92Δ92 mice was 66 days, significantly shorter than that of Eμ-myc/17-92 mice (112 days, p<0.0001).
evidence: Stated directly in text with statistical significance.

claim: mir-17-92Mut92 phenocopied mir-17-92Δ92 in vivo, significantly enhancing the oncogenic cooperation with c-Myc without altering the level of any remaining mir-17-92 components.
source: The resulting mir-17-92Mut92 phenocopied mir-17-92Δ92 in vivo (Figure 1C), significantly enhancing the oncogenic cooperation with c-Myc without altering the level of any remaining mir-17-92 components (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figures 1C and 1D showing survival and expression data.

claim: Mutations of miR-20 or miR-17 failed to affect oncogenesis in the Eμ-myc model.
source: Mutations of miR-20 or miR-17 failed to affect oncogenesis in the Eμ-myc model (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and data not shown)
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Mutations of both miR-19 miRNAs nearly abolished the oncogenic cooperation between mir-17-92 and c-Myc.
source: mutations of both miR-19 miRNAs nearly abolished this oncogenic cooperation (Olive et al., 2009).
evidence: Stated with citation to prior work.

claim: The greater oncogenic activity of mir-17-92Mut92 in comparison with mir-17-92 was consistent with mir-17-92Mut92 preferentially transforming IgM negative progenitor B-cells, and mir-17-92 frequently transforming IgM positive B-cells.
source: The greater oncogenic activity of mir-17-92Mut92 in comparison with mir-17-92 was consistent with mir-17-92Mut92 preferentially transforming IgM negative progenitor B-cells, and mir-17-92 frequently transforming IgM positive B-cells (Figure 2A; Table 1).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 2A and Table 1 showing immunophenotyping data.

claim: Eμ-myc/17-92Δ92 and Eμ-myc/17-92Mut92 mice developed more aggressive B-lymphomas, characterized by massive lymph node enlargement, splenic hyperplasia, leukemia, and widespread dissemination into visceral organs outside of the lymphoid compartment.
source: In comparison to Eμ-myc/17-92 mice, both Eμ-myc/17-92Δ92 and Eμ-myc/17-92Mut92 mice developed more aggressive B-lymphomas, characterized by massive lymph node enlargement, splenic hyperplasia, leukemia, and widespread dissemination into visceral organs outside of the lymphoid compartment (Figure 2B, data not shown).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 2B showing histology.

claim: The control Eμ-myc/MSCV lymphomas invariably exhibited a high proliferation index accompanied by extensive cell death, as evidenced by the widespread 'starry sky' pathology and cleaved caspase 3 staining.
source: The control Eμ-myc/MSCV lymphomas invariably exhibited a high proliferation index accompanied by extensive cell death, as evidenced by the widespread 'starry sky' pathology (Figure 2C,D) and cleaved caspase 3 staining (Figure 2C,E).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figures 2C, 2D, and 2E showing histology and quantification.

claim: The potent oncogenic activity of mir-17-92Δ92 and mir-17-92Mut92 was consistent with the strong reduction of apoptosis in the lymph node tumors.
source: The potent oncogenic activity of mir-17-92Δ92 and mir-17-92Mut92 was consistent with the strong reduction of apoptosis in the lymph node tumors.
evidence: Stated in text and supported by histological data in Figure 2C-E.

claim: The intact miR-92 significantly attenuated the repression of c-Myc-induced apoptosis by mir-17-92 in vivo.
source: In comparison, the intact miR-92 significantly attenuated the repression of c-Myc-induced apoptosis by mir-17-92 in vivo (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figures 2C-E showing apoptosis measurements.

claim: miR-92 overexpression significantly enhanced c-Myc-induced apoptosis in vivo in the Eμ-myc model.
source: In the Eμ-myc model, miR-92 overexpression significantly enhanced c-Myc-induced apoptosis in vivo (Figure 3A,B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figures 3A, 3B, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A showing apoptosis data.

claim: miR-92 overexpression was consistent with a rapid depletion of miR-92-infected cells in premalignant Eμ-myc B-cells.
source: consistent with a rapid depletion of miR-92-infected cells in premalignant Eμ-myc B-cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1B showing cell depletion data.

claim: Enforced miR-92 expression in R26MER/MER MEFs invariably enhanced Myc-induced apoptosis.
source: Enforced miR-92 expression in R26MER/MER MEFs invariably enhanced Myc-induced apoptosis (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C showing apoptosis data.

claim: miR-92 unexpectedly enhanced c-Myc-induced cell proliferation.
source: In addition to promoting c-Myc-induced apoptosis, miR-92 unexpectedly enhanced c-Myc-induced cell proliferation.
evidence: Stated in text and supported by BrdU incorporation data in Figure 3D.

claim: A significant increase of BrdU incorporation was observed in R26MER/MER MEFs overexpressing miR-92, both under normal culture conditions and, more evidently, under serum starvation.
source: A significant increase of BrdU incorporation was observed in R26MER/MER MEFs overexpressing miR-92, both under normal culture conditions and, more evidently, under serum starvation (Figure 3D).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 3D showing BrdU incorporation data.

claim: miR-92 deficiency significantly compromised the ability of mir-17-92 to promote cell cycle progression in B-cells.
source: In addition, miR-92 deficiency significantly compromised the ability of mir-17-92 to promote cell cycle progression in B-cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1D showing BrdU incorporation data.

claim: miR-92 is a unique mir-17-92 component that functionally couples c-Myc-induced cell proliferation and c-Myc-induced apoptosis in the B-cell compartment.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that miR-92 is a unique mir-17-92 component that functionally couples c-Myc-induced cell proliferation and c-Myc-induced apoptosis in the B-cell compartment.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the proliferation and apoptosis data presented.

claim: miR-92-upregulated genes were significantly enriched for the cell cycle pathway, including ccnd1, ccnb1, ccnb2, cdc25b, cdc25c, and cdk4.
source: miR-92-upregulated genes were significantly enriched for the cell cycle pathway, including ccnd1, ccnb1, ccnb2, cdc25b, cdc25c, and cdk4 (Figure 4A,B)
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 4A,B showing microarray pathway analysis.

claim: Genes upregulated by miR-92 were also enriched for the p53 pathway, including the classic p53 target mdm2, as well as the pro-apoptotic p53 targets—noxa, bax, puma, perp, and bid.
source: Genes upregulated by miR-92 were also enriched for the p53 pathway, including the classic p53 target mdm2, as well as the pro-apoptotic p53 targets—noxa, bax, puma, perp, and bid (Figure 4A,B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figures 4A,B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A showing microarray data.

claim: miR-92 overexpression alone caused significant accumulation of Arf mRNA and protein in both R26MER/MER MEFs and wild-type primary B-cells.
source: In both R26MER/MER MEFs and wild-type primary B-cells, miR-92 overexpression alone caused significant accumulation of Arf mRNA and protein (Figure 4C,D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figures 4C,D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C showing RT-PCR and western blot data.

claim: miR-92 overexpression caused rapid stabilization of the p53 protein without alteration of p53 mRNA.
source: consistent with the rapid stabilization of the p53 protein (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C) without alteration of p53 mRNA (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figures 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D showing protein and mRNA data.

claim: Knockdown of p53 in R26MER/MER MEFs completely abolished the effect of miR-92 to enhance c-Myc-induced apoptosis.
source: Knockdown of p53 in R26MER/MER MEFs not only led to a suppression of c-Myc-induced apoptosis, but also completely abolished the effect of miR-92 to enhance c-Myc-induced apoptosis (Figure 4E).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 4E showing apoptosis data with p53 knockdown.

claim: An intact p53 pathway is required for the apoptotic effect of miR-92.
source: These findings suggested that an intact p53 pathway is required for the apoptotic effect of miR-92.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on p53 knockdown experiments.

claim: The miR-92 induction of the pro-apoptotic genes, including noxa, perp, and mdm2, was mediated by the intact p53.
source: Consistently, the miR-92 induction of the pro-apoptotic genes, including noxa, perp, and mdm2, also was mediated by the intact p53 (Figure 4F).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 4F showing gene expression data with p53 knockdown.

claim: miR-92 expression significantly enhanced c-Myc protein level both in MEFs and in primary B-cells without affecting the c-myc mRNA level.
source: Intriguingly, miR-92 expression significantly enhanced c-Myc protein level both in MEFs and in primary B-cells (Figure 5A), without affecting the c-myc mRNA level (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, data not shown).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A showing protein and mRNA data.

claim: miR-92 overexpression in R26MER/MER MEFs stabilized the MycERT2 protein.
source: Consistent with the stabilization of endogenous c-Myc, miR-92 overexpression in R26MER/MER MEFs stabilized the MycERT2 protein (Figure 5B).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5B showing protein turnover data.

claim: fbw7 contains two miR-92 target sites within its 3′UTR.
source: Real-time PCR analysis of these candidate genes confirmed fbw7 (F-box and WD repeat domain-containing 7) as a likely target of miR-92 (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C). fbw7, which contains two miR-92 target sites within its 3′UTR (Figure 5C)
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5C showing the target sites.

claim: A luciferase reporter or a FLAG-tagged fbw7-encoding ORF, when fused to the wild-type fbw7 3′ UTR, were both significantly repressed in a miR-92 dependent manner.
source: A luciferase reporter or a FLAG-tagged fbw7-encoding ORF (open reading frame), when fused to the wild-type fbw7 3′ UTR, were both significantly repressed in a miR-92 dependent manner (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D showing luciferase and western blot data.

claim: Enforced miR-92 expression failed to repress the luciferase reporter that contained an fbw7 3′UTR with two mutated miR-92 binding sites.
source: Yet enforced miR-92 expression failed to repress the luciferase reporter that contained an fbw7 3′UTR with two mutated miR-92 binding sites (Figure 5D), suggesting that miR-92 binding to fbw7 3′UTR is required for this repression.
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5D showing luciferase data with mutated binding sites.

claim: miR-92 effectively repressed endogenous Fbw7 protein level, as demonstrated by the decreased fbw7 mRNA level and Fbw7 immunoprecipitation.
source: Furthermore, miR-92 effectively repressed endogenous Fbw7 protein level, as demonstrated by the decreased fbw7 mRNA level and Fbw7 immunoprecipitation (Figure 5E).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5E showing mRNA and protein data.

claim: Enforced miR-92 expression upregulated multiple Fbw7 substrates at their protein levels, including c-Myc and cyclinE.
source: Consistent with fbw7 as an important target for miR-92, enforced miR-92 expression upregulated multiple Fbw7 substrates at their protein levels, including c-Myc and cyclinE (Figure 5F).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5F showing protein and kinase activity data.

claim: Acute fbw7 knockdown in R26MER/MER MEFs partially phenocopied the effect of miR-92 to enhance c-Myc-induced apoptosis.
source: Functionally, acute fbw7 knockdown in R26MER/MER MEFs partially phenocopied the effect of miR-92 to enhance c-Myc-induced apoptosis (Figure 5G, Figure 5—figure supplement 1G)
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1G showing apoptosis data.

claim: Overexpression of an fbw7α open reading frame completely abolished the apoptotic effect of miR-92.
source: while overexpression of an fbw7α open reading frame (ORF), albeit above its physiological level, completely abolished this apoptotic effect of miR-92 (Figure 5H, Figure 5—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1H showing apoptosis data.

claim: Co-expression of miR-19 and miR-92 as a dicistron attenuated the apoptotic effect of miR-92 in premalignant Eμ-myc B-cells in vivo.
source: Consistent with the opposing effects of miR-19 and miR-92, co-expression of these two miRNAs as a dicistron attenuated the apoptotic effect of miR-92 in premalignant Eμ-myc B-cells in vivo (Figure 6A,B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figures 6A,B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A showing apoptosis data.

claim: A similar antagonistic interaction between miR-19 and miR-92 was observed in R26MER/MER MEFs.
source: A similar antagonistic interaction was also observed in R26MER/MER MEFs; and introducing a miR-19b mutation within mir-19b-92 dicistron abolished this interaction (Figure 6C).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 6C showing apoptosis data in MEFs.

claim: When miR-92 was co-expressed with miR-19, there was a decreased p53 induction and an unaltered c-Myc level.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, we observed a decreased p53 induction and an unaltered c-Myc level when miR-92 was co-expressed with miR-19 (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B showing western blot data.

claim: In Xenopus laevis, miR-19 and miR-92 have identical sequence to their mammalian orthologs.
source: In Xenopus laevis, miR-19 and miR-92 have identical sequence to their mammalian orthologs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B showing sequence alignment.

claim: Individual injection of miR-19 promoted cell survival of hydroxyurea-treated Xenopus embryos, while co-injection of miR-19a and miR-92 significantly attenuated this pro-survival effect.
source: Individual injection of miR-19 promoted cell survival of hydroxyurea-treated Xenopus embryos, while co-injection of miR-19a and miR-92 significantly attenuated this pro-survival effect (Figure 6E).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 6E showing Xenopus embryo survival data.

claim: The functional antagonism between miR-19 and miR-92 was specific, since co-injection of other mir-17-92 components or a mutated miR-92 did not yield any functional interactions in combination with miR-19.
source: This functional antagonism was specific for miR-92 and miR-19, since co-injection of other mir-17-92 components or a mutated miR-92 did not yield any functional interactions in combination with miR-19 (Figure 6F).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 6F showing Xenopus embryo survival data.

claim: The levels of miR-19a, miR-19b, and miR-92 were elevated in both premalignant and malignant Eμ-myc B-cells compared to normal splenic B-cells.
source: Comparing to normal splenic B-cells, the levels of all three mature miRNA species were elevated in both premalignant and malignant Eμ-myc B-cells, possibly due to transcriptional activation of mir-17-92 by c-Myc (Donnell et al., 2005).
evidence: Stated in text with citation and supported by data in Figure 7A.

claim: The miR-19 to miR-92 ratios significantly increased during c-Myc-induced lymphomagenesis.
source: However, the miR-19 to miR-92 ratios significantly increased during c-Myc-induced lymphomagenesis (Figure 7B).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 7B showing ratio data.

claim: When normalized to the respective miRNA levels in normal splenic B-cells, mature miR-19 (including miR-19a and miR-19b) exhibited a greater increase in premalignant and malignant Eμ-myc B-cells than mature miR-92.
source: In other words, when normalized to the respective miRNA levels in normal splenic B-cells, mature miR-19 (including miR-19a and miR-19b) exhibited a greater increase in premalignant and malignant Eμ-myc B-cells than mature miR-92 (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figures 7A-C showing expression data.

claim: This differential increase of miR-19 and miR-92 was also observed in human Burkitt's lymphoma cell lines when compared to normal B-cells isolated from the periphery blood.
source: This differential increase of miR-19 and miR-92 was also observed in human Burkitt's lymphoma cell lines when compared to normal B-cells isolated from the periphery blood (Figure 7D).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 7D showing expression data in human cells.

claim: In the LT2-MYC murine model of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), miR-19a and miR-19b exhibited a stronger increase than miR-92 when comparing tumor cells and the normal counterpart.
source: In the LT2-MYC murine model of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), where tumor development was initiated by tetracycline-inducible c-Myc expression, miR-19a and miR-19b also exhibited a stronger increase than miR-92 when comparing tumor cells and the normal counterpart (Figure 7E).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 7E showing expression data in HCC model.

claim: miR-92 is evolutionarily conserved in Deuterostome (including vertebrates and chordates), Ecdysozoa (including flies and worms), and Lophotrochozoa, yet the remaining mir-17-92 components are only found in vertebrates.
source: miR-92 is evolutionary conserved in Deuterostome (including vertebrates and chordates), Ecdysozoa (including flies and worms), and Lophotrochozoa, yet the remaining mir-17-92 components are only found in vertebrates (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C showing evolutionary conservation.

claim: The polycistronic mir-17-92 employs an antagonistic interaction among its encoded miRNA components to confer an intricate crosstalk between the oncogene and tumor suppressor networks.
source: Thus, the polycistronic mir-17-92 employs an antagonistic interaction among its encoded miRNA components to confer an intricate crosstalk between the oncogene and tumor suppressor networks.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the Introduction based on the findings presented.

claim: fbw7 is the substrate recognition component of an SCF-type E3 ubiquitin ligase that mediates the degradation of several proto-oncoproteins, including Myc, Cyclin E, c-Jun, and Notch.
source: fbw7, which contains two miR-92 target sites within its 3′UTR (Figure 5C), is the substrate recognition component of an SCF-type E3 ubiquitin ligase that mediates the degradation of several proto-oncoproteins, including Myc, Cyclin E, c-Jun, and Notch (Welcker and Clurman, 2008; Crusio et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: The acute inactivation of tumor suppressor Fbw7 imposes a strong oncogenic stress to induce p53-dependent apoptosis, conferring a selective advantage to cells with deficient p53 function.
source: Recent findings indicate that the acute inactivation of tumor suppressor Fbw7 imposes a strong oncogenic stress to induce p53-dependent apoptosis, conferring a selective advantage to cells with deficient p53 function (Minella et al., 2007; Onoyama et al., 2007; Matsuoka et al., 2008; Grim et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: The p53-dependent apoptosis induced by Fbw7 inactivation is, at least in part, due to an aberrant increase of c-Myc dosage.
source: This p53-dependent apoptosis is, at least in part, due to an aberrant increase of c-Myc dosage (Onoyama et al., 2007; Matsuoka et al., 2008).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior literature.

claim: miR-92 overexpression significantly increased the c-Myc protein level in wild-type Hct116 cells, but not in FBW7−/− Hct116 cells.
source: In support of this hypothesis, miR-92 overexpression significantly increased the c-Myc protein level in wild-type Hct116 cells, but not in FBW7−/− Hct116 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F), suggesting FBW7 was essential for miR-92 to induce c-MYC increase.
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1F showing western blot data.

claim: There was an inverse correlation between the level of miR-92 and fbw7 when comparing Eμ-myc/17-92Δ92 and Eμ-myc/17-92 lymphoma cells.
source: Observations from our in vivo experiments also supported this post-transcriptional regulation of Fbw7 by miR-92, as we observed an inverse correlation between the level of miR-92 and fbw7 when comparing Eμ-myc/17-92Δ92 and Eμ-myc/17-92 lymphoma cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Stated in text with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1E showing expression data.

claim: The miR-92-Fbw7-Myc axis constitutes a major mechanism underlying the pro-apoptotic effects of miR-92.
source: Despite these caveats, our results strongly argue that the miR-92-Fbw7 axis constitutes a major mechanism underlying the pro-apoptotic effects of miR-92.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the functional studies presented.

claim: The activation of AKT signaling by miR-19 would lead to increased phosphorylation of Mdm2, thus destabilizing p53 to dampen the apoptotic response induced by miR-92.
source: Since miR-19 represses pten to promote the PI3K/AKT pathway, the activation of AKT signaling would lead to increased phosphorylation of Mdm2, thus destabilizing p53 to dampen the apoptotic response induced by miR-92 (Gottlieb et al., 2002; Ogawara et al., 2002).
evidence: Stated with citations to prior literature explaining the mechanism.

claim: The functional readout of miR-92 heavily depends on cell types and biological contexts.
source: The functional readout of miR-92 heavily depends on cell types and biological contexts.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section.

claim: miR-92 is not a tumor suppressor miRNA.
source: It is important to recognize that miR-92 is not a tumor suppressor miRNA.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Like c-Myc, miR-92 elicits potent oncogene stress to engage tumor suppressor response, at least in part, by activating p53.
source: Like c-Myc, miR-92 elicits potent oncogene stress to engage tumor suppressor response, at least in part, by activating p53.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section based on the data presented.

claim: Under contexts when proliferation becomes a rate-limiting event for oncogenesis, or when p53-dependent apoptosis is compromised, miR-92 could render a pro-proliferative effect that is strictly oncogenic.
source: Under other contexts when proliferation becomes a rate-limiting event for oncogenesis, or when p53-dependent apoptosis is compromised, miR-92 could render a pro-proliferative effect that is strictly oncogenic (Tsuchida et al., 2011).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with citation.

claim: The miR-19:miR-92 antagonism constitutes a novel mechanism to confer an intricate balance between oncogene signaling and innate tumor suppressor responses.
source: The miR-19:miR-92 antagonism constitutes a novel mechanism to confer an intricate balance between oncogene signaling and innate tumor suppressor responses (Figure 7F).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section with reference to Figure 7F showing a model.

claim: An increase in the miR-19:miR-92 ratio is likely to favor the suppression of c-Myc-induced apoptosis and to promote oncogenesis.
source: This balance can be disrupted in premalignant and malignant cells that exhibit c-Myc overexpression, as an increase in the miR-19:miR-92 ratio is likely to favor the suppression of c-Myc-induced apoptosis and to promote oncogenesis.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section based on the expression data.

claim: Different changes of miR-19 vs miR-92 during oncogenesis could be a result of differential miRNA biogenesis and/or turn-over.
source: Although all mir-17-92 components are co-transcriptionally regulated, different changes of miR-19 vs miR-92 during oncogenesis could be a result of differential miRNA biogenesis and/or turn-over.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section as a possible explanation.

claim: Specific RNA-binding proteins, such as hnRNP A1, promote the processing of a specific mir-17-92 component, miR-18.
source: It has been shown that specific RNA-binding proteins, such as hnRNP A1, promote the processing of a specific mir-17-92 component, miR-18 (Guil and Cáceres, 2007).
evidence: Stated with citation to prior literature.

claim: The functional antagonism between the more ancient miR-92 and the newly evolved mir-19 might result from the convergence of these two separate evolutionary paths at the origin of vertebrates.
source: The functional antagonism between the more ancient miR-92 and the newly evolved mir-19 might result from the convergence of these two separate evolutionary paths at the origin of vertebrates.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section as a hypothesis.

claim: The complex interactions among polycistronic miRNA components can coordinate and balance a multitude of cellular and molecular processes during normal development and disease.
source: It is likely that the complex interactions among polycistronic miRNA components can coordinate and balance a multitude of cellular and molecular processes during normal development and disease.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section as a general principle.

claim: A crosstalk between oncogene and tumor suppressor pathways has been hardwired through evolution into the unique gene structure of a polycistronic oncomir.
source: Thus, our studies suggest a novel mechanism by which a crosstalk between oncogene and tumor suppressor pathways has been hardwired through evolution into the unique gene structure of a polycistronic oncomir.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion.
